messages:
maya (Product): Quick sync — thinking through the model catalog filter bar and compare table. Two quick asks: 1) make performance badges clearer at small widths, 2) version pinning affordance when you open compare.

Dave (Design): Agree. On badges: right now the green/yellow/red circles are tiny and rely on color alone. We should add a microlabel (e.g., 'fast', 'ok', 'slow') that appears at <= 720px or on hover.

anu (DevEx): Microlabel sounds good. Also we could surface a tooltip with median p50/p95 numbers. That helps engineers trust the badge instead of guessing.

benji (Eng): We can expose p50/p95 from the API, but it increases payload size. Suggest lazy-load tooltips via XHR when the user hovers so table first paints fast.

maya (Product): Lazy-load tooltips is a good compromise. For the microlabel copy, prefer 1 word. Ideas: 'fast' / 'typical' / 'slow' or 'low' / 'med' / 'high' latency?

Dave (Design): Lean toward 'fast'/'typical'/'slow' since it's user-facing. 'Low/med/high' reads like resource not UX.

aria (Accessibility): If we add microlabels, ensure they're text (not only color). Also need accessible name for the badge: `aria-label="inference latency: p50 60ms, p95 220ms"`. Keyboard users should be able to focus the badge and trigger the tooltip (Enter/Space).

anu (DevEx): Noted. We'll add focusable elements and keyboard handlers that load the info.

benji (Eng): About version pinning — current design shows a pin icon only in the row actions. Problem: when you compare two models side-by-side it's unclear which version is pinned vs the catalog default. Suggest a small pinned-chip next to the model name: "Pinned v3.2.1" with subtle background.

Dave (Design): I sketched two options: chip inline vs a sticky header that lists pinned versions for the compare set. Inline chip is simpler for users scanning rows; sticky header helps when comparing many models.

maya (Product): Inline chip + hover reveal of pin metadata (who pinned, when) should cover 90% of needs. Sticky header could be a follow-up if customers ask.

aria (Accessibility): Make sure pinned-chip has an accessible label like `aria-label=\"pinned model version 3.2.1 (pinned by maya)\"` and can be toggled via keyboard. Also color contrast for chip bg/text must meet 4.5:1.

Dave (Design): For color tokens I'm proposing `--badge-bg-fast: #E6FBF1` with text `#036B3C` (contrast checks out) and `--chip-bg: #F5F7FF` with text `#0B2B66`. Will run into trouble on dark mode — need tokens for both themes.

benji (Eng): We already have theme tokens. I'll wire these and add the lazy tooltip endpoint `/api/catalog/model_latency?model_id=...&metric=p95`. It returns minimal JSON: `\{"p50\": 62, \"p95\": 210\}`.

anu (DevEx): Small nit on copy for the tooltip header: prefer "Observed latency" instead of just "Latency" so it's clear it's measured.

maya (Product): Good call. Last item: on mobile/tablet the compare table collapses into cards. We should show microbadge + pinned-chip at the top of each card. Dave — can you update the spec for the card layout?

Dave (Design): Yep, I'll push adjustments to Figma and add a small motion for the tooltip on tap.

maya (Product): Thanks folks. Action items: Dave update figma (due EOD), Benji add lazy tooltip API + keyboard support (PR next week), Anu wire keyboard handlers and analytics event for pin toggles, Aria to review contrast and aria-labels after PR.

design-bot: new Figma file uploaded: "catalog/perf-badges-and-pins-v2"

maya (Product): Awesome — check Figma, leave comments on specifics. :thumbsup:

aria (Accessibility): I'll run an axe check on the next build once PRs land.

benji (Eng): I'll post PR link when ready.

maya (Product): Great. Meeting done.
